$what: Dead hrefs that are ALREADY dead at the recorded commit and were never fixed. They are NOT forgiven -- they are enumerated so that "net new = 0" is a reachable, violable predicate instead of a permanently red one.
$predicate: net_new = current_dead_set MINUS this set, compared item-by-item on (page, href). net_new > 0 -> exit 1. net_new = 0 -> exit 0.
$how_to_raise: node tools/_check_links_exist.mjs --emit-baseline tools/data/known-failures-links.json -- commit that single file on its own. Raising the baseline is only legitimate when the new entry is itself a known/accepted failure; it is NEVER a way to make a red gate green.
$how_to_revoke_one_entry: Fix the dead link on the page, re-run the gate (the entry will then be reported as RESOLVED), and delete that one entry in its own commit. Entries are never auto-deleted by the gate -- deletion is always a human action.
$how_to_shrink_the_file: Every removed entry is a real fix. An entry that is no longer failing is reported as RESOLVED and left in place on purpose, so the diff that shrinks this file is always a human decision.
$registration_note: HAND-REGISTERED, not emitted by --emit-baseline. Only the 2 pairs whose target genuinely exists under static/ are recorded. The other 33 net-new pairs at the same commit are REAL link-form defects (./ vs ../ and trailing-slash forms in newly written v1.3.15 architecture pages) and are deliberately NOT registered: emitting the whole dead set here would be using the baseline to make a red gate green, which this file forbids.
$does_not_affect: tools/audit-links.mjs -- it reads NO baseline at all (grep -nE known|baseline|allow|failures tools/audit-links.mjs returns nothing), so audit-links BROKEN_LINKS is UNCHANGED by this registration. audit-links and _check_links_exist are two different rulers with different predicates.

$prior_history.note: This file previously reached zero at commit 7eaa634c3f3cb4c8bf1804b3496520f82ac0a4f9 (162 entries, all fixed not forgiven). It is no longer empty; see $registration_note.

recordedAt.note: Recorded by hand. Values here are DATA, reviewed like any other data change.

known.note: Pre-existing dead href recorded as a KNOWN FAILURE. Revoke = fix the link on the page, then delete THIS entry alone in its own commit (never bundled with unrelated work). WHY ACCEPTED: Target EXISTS at static/v1.3.15/{en,zh}/native-1.3.15-src/ALL-FUNCTIONS-LIST.txt (166428 B). Zola publishes static/ verbatim -- established by an INDEPENDENT POSITIVE CONTROL, not by trusting documentation: a minimal fixture with static/probe.txt and static/sub/dir/nested.txt produced public/probe.txt and public/sub/dir/nested.txt byte-identical after `zola build` (zola 0.22.1). So /v1.3.15/{en,zh}/native-1.3.15-src/ALL-FUNCTIONS-LIST.txt is reachable on a COMPLETED build. Both rulers (audit-links.mjs, _check_links_exist.mjs) resolve targets only under content/, which is the ruler coverage gap, not a content defect. CAVEAT RECORDED: the public/ tree on disk at registration time came from a KILLED build and contains no static/ files at all (not even shell.css), so it is NOT evidence either way -- the fixture control is what settles it.
